sites.tag_type: HiBiT (11 aa) and V5 (14 aa), each with GGG linker
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Luminescence detected on live iPSCs via HiBiT/LgBiT complementation, confirming surface display of the tagged full-length protein (L1, L2). No complement-inhibition or T-cell costimulation assay reported; L3 provides a rationale that tagging is unlikely to perturb these functions but does not measure them.
sites.rationale: All six ledger lines (L1–L6) converge on a single junction: the tag is inserted after the signal peptide and before the mature extracellular domain of full-length, membrane-anchored CD46. The topology landmarks fix the SP boundary at residue 34 (A34), making insert_after_residue=34 the computed junction; residue_before=A (pos 34) and residue_after=C (pos 35) were read directly from the numbered sequence. Because the paper names the landmark (signal peptide cleavage site) rather than a residue number, the position is topology_derived. CD46 has exactly one extracellular terminus (N-terminal, after SP; the C-terminus is intracellular at 367–392), so there is no ambiguity. Both HiBiT and V5 constructs were placed at this same junction in independent HDR templates. CRISPR HDR knock-in of HiBiT or V5 tag (each followed by a GGG linker) into full-length, membrane-anchored CD46 in human iPSCs. L4 specifies the tag must be placed after the signal peptide to avoid cleavage; L5 specifies a GGG linker between the tag and the start of the extracellular portion; L6 describes two 200 bp HDR templates (one HiBiT, one V5) encoding this design. The SP boundary is residue 34 per the topology landmarks, placing the junction between A34 and C35.

sources.claim: Consequently, the tag has to be knocked in after the signal peptide to avoid downstream removal.

literature_notes: All six ledger lines derive from a single publication (PMC6640264) and describe one experimental design: CRISPR HDR knock-in of a short peptide tag (HiBiT or V5, each ~11–14 aa, with a GGG linker) immediately after the signal peptide of full-length CD46. Because both tags target the identical junction and the paper names the SP boundary rather than a residue number, this is reported as one topology_derived site. No internal extracellular loop insertions, no intracellular insertions, and no function-abrogating positions are described anywhere in the ledger, so other_positions is empty. The ledger contains no evidence for any other junction in CD46.
